6. Date of passing of impugned 16.03.2024 order [2024:RJ-JD:41252] (2 of 4)
[CRLMB-5894/2024]
2.
It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4. I have considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the material available on record.
The first bail application came to be dismissed by this Court while giving a liberty to the petitioner to renew the prayer for bail after recording of the statement of the victim in the trial court.
Now she has been examined in court, thus, the instant bail plea.

After going through her statement recorded during trial and during investigation, it is felt that there is a substance in the submission of learned counsel Mr. Rahul Sharma that the victim was a consenting party.

Learned counsel drew the Court's attention towards the statement made by her in cross-examination where she admits that when the accused surreptitiously entered into her house and established physical relation and went out, she neither raised any hue and cry nor any complaint was made to anyone.

The clandestine manner in which, she kept silence for a long time [2024:RJ-JD:41252] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-5894/2024] is persuading this Court to tentatively accept the plea that she was a consenting party, however, the same is not the final opinion of this Court and it is made only with a view to justifiably dispose of the bail application.

As far as the age of victim is concerned, learned counsel would contend that the requisite academic record has not been collected by the investigating agency and now in absence whereof, it cannot be said with utmost certainty that she was below the age of 18 years when she complained of sexual abuse.
I have gone through the record.
There is a photocopy of Sky Wing International School and which is reflecting a mark-sheet of class 8 th.

No birth certificate, no certificate of department of statistic and no copy of death and birth register of panchayat/municipality and even any document relating to school first attended has been placed on record.
Now it is a moot question and which shall be open for the trial court to adjudicate in the trial whether the victim was below 18 years of age at the relevant time.

Since the petitioner is languishing in jail for last one year and nine months and he is a teenage boy and now the girl has been examined in the trial, therefore, any apprehension of her tempering and hampering is ruled out and there is high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude
, therefore, in light of these facts and circumstances, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.

Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he Virat vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:41252) on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120273315/
2 furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.
(FARJAND ALI),J 334-chhavi/-
